content: The text provided is a long list of references and guidelines related to obstetrics, gynecology, and maternal health. It includes studies, systematic reviews, clinical trials, and WHO recommendations on various aspects of childbirth, labor management, maternal care, and neonatal outcomes. 1. Chen HF and Chu KK developed a double-lined nomogram for cervical dilation in Chinese primigravidas, published in Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand in 1986. 2. Diegmann EK, Andrews CM, and Niemczura CA studied the duration of the second stage of labor in uncomplicated, nulliparous African American and Puerto Rican women, published in J Midwifery Womens Health in 2000. 3. Dior U, Kogan L, Ezra Y, and Calderon-Margalit R analyzed population-based labor curves, as reported in Am J Obstet Gynecol in 2013. 4. Duignan NM, Studd JW, and Hughes AO examined the characteristics of normal labor across different racial groups, published in Br J Obstet Gynaecol in 1975. 5. Shi Q, Tan XQ, Liu XR, Tian XB, and Qi HB investigated labor patterns in Chinese women in Chongqing, published in BJOG in 2016. 6. Studd J discussed the use of partograms and nomograms of cervical dilation in managing primigravid labor, as published in Br Med J. 7. Studd J, Clegg DR, Sanders RR, and Hughes AO identified high-risk labors using labor nomograms, published in Br Med J in 1975. 8. Wüstemann M, Gremm B, Scharf A, and Sohn C evaluated the influence of the walking epidural on labor duration and vaginal operative delivery rates, published in Gynäkologische Praxis in 2003. 9. Gibb DM, Cardozo LD, Studd JW, Magos AL, and Cooper DJ studied the outcomes of spontaneous labor in multigravidae, published in Br J Obstet Gynaecol in 1982. 10. Gupta J, Sood A, Hofmeyr G, and Vogel J reviewed positions during the second stage of labor for women without epidural anesthesia, as part of the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 11. Lawrence A, Lewis L, Hofmeyr GJ, and Styles C examined maternal positions and mobility during the first stage of labor, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2013. 12. Elvander C, Ahlberg M, Thies-Lagergren L, Cnattingius S, and Stephansson O conducted a population-based study on birth positions and obstetric anal sphincter injuries in 113,000 spontaneous births, published in BMC Pregnancy Childbirth in 2015. 13. Zileni BD, Glover P, Jones M, Teoh KK, Zileni CW, and Muller A surveyed Malawian women's knowledge and use of labor and birthing positions, published in Women Birth in 2017. 14. Okonta P explored birthing positions and the awareness and preferences of pregnant women in a developing country, published in the Internet J Gynecol Obstet in 2012. 15. Kibuka M and Thornton JG reviewed positions during the second stage of labor for women with epidural anesthesia, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 16. Lemos A, Amorim MM, Dornelas de Andrade A, de Souza AI, Cabral Filho JE, and Correia JB analyzed pushing and bearing-down methods during the second stage of labor, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 17. Bergstrom L, Seidel L, Skillman-Hull L, and Roberts J studied social interactions during the transition from the first to the second stage of labor, published in Birth in 1997. 18. Fraser W, Marcoux S, Krauss I, Douglas J, Goulet C, Boulvain M, et al. conducted a multicenter randomized controlled trial on delayed pushing for nulliparous women in the second stage of labor with continuous epidural analgesia, published in Am J Gynecol Obstet in 2000. 19. Aasheim V, Nilsen ABV, Reinar LM, and Lukasse M reviewed perineal techniques during the second stage of labor to reduce perineal trauma, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 20. Priddis H, Schmied V, and Dahlen H conducted a qualitative study on women's experiences following severe perineal trauma, published in BMC Womens Health in 2014. 21. Borghi J, Bastus S, Belizan M, Carroli G, Hutton G, and Fox-Rushby J analyzed the costs of publicly provided maternity services in Rosario, Argentina, published in Salud Publica Mex in 2003. 22. Labrecque M, Eason E, and Marcoux S explored women's views on prenatal perineal massage, published in Br J Obstet Gynaecol in 2001. 23. Stamp G and Kruzins GS surveyed midwives who participated in a randomized trial of perineal massage during labor, published in Austral J Midwifery in 2001. 24. Jiang H, Qian X, Carroli G, and Garner P compared selective versus routine use of episiotomy for vaginal birth, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 25. Amorim MM, Coutinho IC, Melo I, and Katz L conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing selective episiotomy to a non-episiotomy protocol, published in Reprod Health in 2017. 26. Borghi J, Fox-Rushby J, Bergel E, Abalos E, Hutton G, and Carroli G evaluated the cost-effectiveness of routine versus restrictive episiotomy in Argentina, published in Am J Obstet Gynecol in 2002. 27. Kettle C, Dowswell T, and Ismail KM reviewed continuous and interrupted suturing techniques for repairing episiotomy or second-degree tears, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 28. Ith P, Dawson A, Homer CS, and Klinken Whelan A studied the practices of skilled birth attendants during labor, birth, and the immediate postpartum period in Cambodia, published in Midwifery in 2013. 29. Miller S, Abalos E, Chamillard M, Ciapponi A, Colaci D, Comande D, et al. proposed a pathway toward evidence-based, respectful maternity care worldwide, published in Lancet in 2016. 30. Chaves SdC, Cecatti JG, Carroli G, Lumbiganon P, Hogue CJ, Mori R, et al. explored pathways for maternal mortality reduction in the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health, published in Rev Panam Salud Publica in 2015. 31. Souza JP, Tunçalp Ö, Vogel JP, Bohren M, Widmer M, Oladapo OT, et al. discussed the obstetric transition and the pathway toward ending preventable maternal deaths, published in BJOG in 2014. 32. Graham ID, Carroli G, Davies C, and Medves JM updated episiotomy rates worldwide, published in Birth in 2005. 33. Diniz SG, d’Oliveira AF, and Lansky S addressed equity and women's health services for contraception, abortion, and childbirth in Brazil, published in Reprod Health Matters in 2012. 34. Okafor I, Ugwu EO, and Obi SN investigated disrespect and abuse during facility-based childbirth in a low-income country, published in Int J Gynaecol Obstet in 2015. 35. Bohren MA, Vogel JP, Tunçalp Ö, Fawole B, Titiloye MA, Olutayo AO, et al. conducted a qualitative study on mistreatment of women during childbirth in Abuja, Nigeria, published in Reprod Health in 2017. 36. Bohren MA, Vogel JP, Hunter EC, Lutsiv O, Makh SK, Souza JP, et al. performed a mixed-methods systematic review on the global mistreatment of women during childbirth in health facilities, published in PLoS Med. 37. Sando D, Ratcliffe H, McDonald K, Spiegelman D, Lyatuu G, Mwanyika-Sando M, et al. studied the prevalence of disrespect and abuse during facility-based childbirth in urban Tanzania, published in BMC Pregnancy Childbirth in 2016. 38. Gülmezoglu AM, Langer A, Piaggio G, Lumbiganon P, Villar J, and Grimshaw J conducted a cluster randomized trial of an educational intervention to improve obstetric practices, published in BJOG in 2007. 39. Hofmeyr GJ, Singata M, Lawrie TA, Vogel JP, Landoulsi S, Seuc AH, et al. developed a study protocol for the Gentle Assisted Pushing (GAP) study to reduce prolonged second-stage labor, published in Reprod Health in 2015. 40. Hofmeyr G, Vogel J, and Cuthbert A reviewed the use of fundal pressure during the second stage of labor, published in the Cochrane Database Systematic Review in 2017. 41. Habek D, Vuković Bobić M, and Hrgović Z assessed the potential clinical risks of the Kristeller maneuver, published in Cent Eur J Med in 2008. 42. Zanconato G, Cavaliere E, Cherubini G, Bortolami O, Mantovani E, Iacovella C, et al. evaluated the prevalence and effects of fundal pressure during labor in current obstetric practice, published in Minerva Ginecol in 2014. 43. Iyengar SD, Iyengar K, Martines JC, Dashora K, and Deora KK studied childbirth practices in rural Rajasthan, India, and their implications for neonatal health and survival, published in J Perinatol in 2008. 44. De Leeuw JW, Vierhout ME, Struijk PC, Hop WC, and Wallenburg HC examined anal sphincter damage after vaginal delivery, its functional outcomes, and risk factors for fecal incontinence, published in Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand in 2001. 45. Declercq ER, Sakala C, Corry MP, and Applebaum SS conducted a survey of women's childbearing experiences in 2006, published in J Perinat Educ in 2007. 46. Goldman N and Glei DA evaluated midwifery care in rural Guatemala, published in Soc Sci Med in 2003. 47. WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage were accessed in December 2017. 48. Guidelines on delayed umbilical cord clamping for improved maternal and infant health outcomes were accessed in December 2017. 49. Guidelines on basic newborn resuscitation were accessed in December 2017. 50. Recommendations for managing common childhood conditions, including newborn care, were accessed in December 2017. 51. WHO recommendations on newborn health and postnatal care were accessed in January 2018. 52. Guidelines on optimal feeding of low birth-weight infants in lowand middle-income countries were accessed in December 2017. 53. Standards for improving maternal and newborn care in health facilities were accessed in December 2017. 54. The WHO Safe Childbirth Checklist program was piloted to improve maternal and newborn health care quality, published in PLoS One in 2012. 55. Brouwers M, Kho M, Browman G, Burgers J, Cluzeau F, Feder G, et al. advanced guideline development and evaluation in healthcare through the AGREE II framework, published in CMAJ in 2010. 56. The GREAT Network website was accessed in October 2017 for resources on improving maternal and newborn care quality.
